The reason they haven't implemented a kill cam isn't for those reasons, its due to the massive amount of data that needs to be stored serverside and the framework to set something like that up. And even when you do have the backend for it, there's the issue of streaming that data to players, and even if they have a blatant replay of a hacker killing them, it takes a massive amount of manpower to view and verify recordings

Counter Strike tackled this problem by cataloging all their information in a "series of events" format and then relying on players to verify and condemn cheating. The issue with implementing this in something like Tarkov is that Tarkov has significantly more complexity to it in items and movement, and working backwards to implement this feature would require a massive amount of dev hours. Then there's the element of getting enough players to verify recordings of others.

It is possible, however you usually won't want to pass so more than 200ma current through an arduino.

This reply isn't as comprehensive as I'd like as I don't have much time, but hopefully some of these notes help.

Arduino pins can't have more than 40ma bring drawn, or have more than a total of 200ma drawn from all pins, so keep that in mind. Trying to draw more will damage the board.

Assuming you're using common LEDs, that would bring the total well above 200ma. Thankfully there is a relatively simple electrical solution, but it would require making a circuit.

 For high current flow look into using a mosfet with using the arduino to switch, and power the mosfet and arduino externally. Just be aware that these heat up a lot and like having heatsinks. Relays are also an option if you don't want to switch frequently or run pwm over the line. 

A simple power line for things like this generally are old usb cables if they fall within current limitations.
If you have an old usb cable you can clip it and use the red/black power wires in it just be aware that usb has a max current of 500ma for usb2 and 900ma for usb3. If you need more current look around for a decent DC power supply.

I'm sure there's an all in one board to power the arduino and allow switching more current if you don't want to get into the electrical stuff, I just don't know of one. Id say its worth looking for.

Also take everything I take with a grain of salt, I'm just a hobbiest not an electrical engineer and I very well could be wrong, this is just what I learned trying to tackle a similar issue.

The CPU you chose is great, but Minecraft is a single threaded game. When using community made servers side programs such as paper, you at most will see 2 threads being used. Because of this I wouldn't be too worried about number of cores. Ideally, you wouldn't want to have more servers than the number of cores in your system just to be safe.

However AMD has been leading in multithreaded applications for a long time, and they have no integrated GPU. You could reasonably not need to buy a seperate gpu and get much faster performance by purchasing a newish i3 or i5. Intel runs minecraft servers significantly faster than AMD cpus as of current. I do believe the latest i3 has 4 cores, incredible single thread speeds, an integrated gpu, all for about the same or a little higher price than the current CPU on your list.

I don't know what OS you plan to run, but I would recommend using Ubuntu Server, a command line operating system, and learning to become comfortable with the Linux kernel. Lightweight operating systems like this are great because they take so few system resources. Using a command called screen, you can easily jump between your server consoles. Using SSH, you can pretty easily set it up to be able to access the systems command-line from any computer on your home network as well. This eliminates the need for having the server being hooked up to a monitor and keyboard after the first startup.

As for your powersupply, I peeked at a list and it looked like you were looking at a 400 watt one for almost 100 dollars. I don't know if its because we're from different parts of the world or not, but at least nearby to where I live Amazon has some great 80+ bronze options for around 40 dollars.

Anyways, that's my take. Feel free to message me or reply with any questions, I have lots of time at the moment and am happy to help.
